notes.heading: What the bar no longer carries

items.text: In December 1973 the American Psychiatric Association's Board of Trustees voted to remove homosexuality from its diagnostic manual.
items.source: Jack Drescher, “Out of DSM: Depathologizing Homosexuality”, Behavioral Sciences 5(4):565–575, 2015 (PMC4695779), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4695779/ read 15 Nov 2026

items.text: In 1987 the last trace, “ego-dystonic homosexuality”, was removed in the manual's revision, DSM-III-R.
items.source: Jack Drescher, “Out of DSM: Depathologizing Homosexuality”, Behavioral Sciences 5(4):565–575, 2015 (PMC4695779), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4695779/ read 15 Nov 2026

items.text: In May 1990 the World Health Organization adopted ICD-10, whose note reads: “Sexual orientation by itself is not to be regarded as a disorder.”
items.source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 (browser, 2019 version), block F66, Note, https://icd.who.int/browse10/2019/en/GetConcept?ConceptId=F66 read 15 Nov 2026; adoption “May 1990 (WHA43.24)”, https://www.who.int/standards/classifications/classification-of-diseases read 15 Nov 2026

notes.heading: The two adverts: what is real and what is invented

items.text: “Mountains of Material” is invented. Its name is the handbook's own phrase for Scripture memorization: “adding mountains of material to your memory tapes”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 130 (PDF p. 138) and p. 132 (PDF p. 140); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: The Pocket Library is invented. The real Exodus booklets were numbered #PR-01 to #PR-13 (© 1993–1998), and an Exodus booklet was priced 1.00 in 1987.
items.source: Exodus International–North America, “Resource Booklets” (the back page printed after each booklet in the series), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 12, PDF p. 13, the codes on the booklets in the folder; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026; Emotional Dependency (Exodus International–North America edition, 1987), back cover, priced “1.00”, Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 9, PDF p. 15, the back cover; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: Their phone numbers are fictional (the 555-01xx range), and no prices are invented: the only price shown, 1.00, is a 1987 Exodus booklet's.
items.source: Exodus International–North America, “Resource Booklets” (the back page printed after each booklet in the series), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 12, PDF p. 13, the codes on the booklets in the folder; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026; Emotional Dependency (Exodus International–North America edition, 1987), back cover, priced “1.00”, Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 9, PDF p. 15, the back cover; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

notes.heading: Left out of the two-minute tape

items.text: Roots and Recovery was a real video, sold for $20 with “an overview of nine proven principles”. The listing even warned that its “product quality is not typical … However, we make this resource available due to the relevance of its message.” This listing is from 2001, after this tape's year.
items.source: Focus on the Family, the truth comes out: The Roots and Causes of Male Homosexuality (© 2001), resources pages, printed p. 39 (PDF p. 22), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 6 Folder 5, the listing “Understanding Homosexuality: Roots and Recovery”; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: The Un-Walk Steps class is invented. Its rules are the Love in Action class manual's own: “There is no free lunch!”, “KEEP A JOURNAL!”, “Be on time!”, “lessons read, homework done, pen and binder in hand”.
items.source: Love in Action, Steps Out Program Class Manual (c. 1994; its latest dated item is June 1994), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 13 Folder 1, Program Overview p. iii (PDF p. 6); Group Interaction p. v (PDF p. 16); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: Women Relating to Men is a real flyer: its title, its two hooks (“I Don't Want To Go To This Class!”, “I Wish I Had Gone To This Class”) and its five topics. Its presenters and its church are not named here.
items.source: The flyer “Women Relating to Men … For All Married and Single Women”, Thursday 11 June 1992, 7:30 P.M., Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 1 Folder 3 (“Women Only”), PDF p. 17, the flyer's text; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: The felt board's strips and both question cards carry the handbook's own words (the questions are its workbook questions 2 and 5). The narrator reads the handbook verbatim or in close paraphrase, and the bar names the page each time.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (a handbook for pastors, counselors and lay workers), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984). Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2, Folder 13. printed pp. 128–133 and 135 (PDF pp. 136–141, 143): chapter thirteen, “Displacement: Putting Off/Putting On” (printed pp. 128–140)

items.text: At the end, booklet one's page shows the narrator's paraphrase of its sentence (“Their claim of not having asked for their orientation is, in most cases, true”) and its own four words, “something they never chose”. The title on its cover, “Born That Way?”, is invented; the page number is the real page's.
items.source: Exodus International–North America, Is Homosexuality Inborn? (resource booklet #PR-01), © 1996. Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2, Folder 12, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 34).

items.text: The break is the handbook's own admission, printed under its heading “Remember Half The Process Won't Work”, in the same chapter as the tape's lessons.
